review_output.summary: [High] browser_class Literal still accepts firefox/webkit, but every launch now passes channel='chrome'
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: BrowserConfig(browser_class='firefox' or 'webkit') still validates and builds per-engine args (browser.py:265-279). The launch at :281-284 passes channel='chrome' to the firefox/webkit launchers with no guard, and patchright targets Chromium only. Two advertised values can no longer launch, and nothing rejects them before runtime. Remedy: narrow the Literal to 'chromium' or add a validator with a clear error, or pass channel only when browser_class == 'chromium'.

review_output.summary: [High] Default Browser() launch hard-codes channel='chrome', requiring system Google Chrome while install docs still say `playwright install chromium`
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the built-in launch path is the default when no cdp/wss/binary path is set (browser.py:296-306). It now requests branded Chrome stable with no config option to opt out. README.md:33, docs/quickstart.mdx:38 and the notebook install only bundled Chromium via playwright, so on CI, Docker or any machine without Chrome the first Agent run fails. Remedy: add a BrowserConfig.channel option or fall back to bundled Chromium, pass the channel only for chromium, and update the install docs to `patchright install chrome`.

review_output.summary: [High] The new kwargs logic in _create_context has no test
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the fixed no_viewport=True / user_agent / bypass_csp call is replaced by three conditional branches. No test checks what browser.new_context receives, and nothing under tests/ calls _create_context. Regressions in viewport, user-agent or CSP-bypass handling would ship unnoticed. Remedy: add a parametrized test in tests/test_context.py with an AsyncMock new_context over headless x user_agent x disable_security, asserting on new_context.call_args.kwargs.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Agent overwrites the user's new_context_config.disable_security by mutating the injected Browser's config
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: both flags default to False. A user who sets only BrowserContextConfig(disable_security=True) has it silently reset to False and loses bypass_csp/ignore_https_errors (context.py:423). The write changes the caller's shared BrowserConfig, which also affects later browser.new_context() calls (browser.py:127). It runs even when a browser_context is injected, and only the Agent path does this sync. Remedy: don't mutate the injected config. Derive the effective value (e.g. model_copy), or propagate only when the field wasn't set explicitly via a BrowserConfig model_validator, or read self.browser.config.disable_security in _create_context.

review_output.summary: [Medium] The new disable_security sync in Agent.__init__ has no test
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: this line decides whether Agent-created contexts get the CSP/HTTPS bypass and overwrites values the caller set explicitly. No test covers it or its precedence, so a broken sync or an unwanted overwrite ships silently. Remedy: add Agent tests with a mocked LLM for both precedence directions (BrowserConfig(disable_security=True), and BrowserConfig(False) with a context config of True), asserting agent.browser_context.config.disable_security.

review_output.summary: [Medium] The no-argument path of new_context() changed, but only the explicit-config path is tested
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: test_new_context_creation (tests/test_browser.py:234) passes an explicit config only. The fixed fallback to self.config.new_context_config, used in docs and fixtures, has no regression test. Remedy: call browser_obj.new_context() with no argument and assert context.config is browser_obj.config.new_context_config.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Nothing checks the new channel='chrome' launch kwarg, and the existing launch mocks reject extra kwargs
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the mocks at tests/test_browser.py:24 and :196 are `launch(self, headless, args, proxy=None)`. The handle_* kwargs already broke them before this change, and channel adds another, so the builtin-launch tests raise TypeError before their assertions. No test asserts the channel, which is also passed for firefox/webkit. Remedy: give the dummy launch a **kwargs parameter, assert kwargs.get('channel') == 'chrome' for chromium, and add a firefox case for the intended behaviour.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Headed mode lost no_viewport=True and now gets the library's default emulated viewport
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the headed window is launched at screen size (browser.py:244-254), but the context no longer sets no_viewport. A fixed emulated viewport (likely 1280x720) sits inside a larger window, which affects screenshots, viewport_expansion filtering and scroll math, and record_video_size no longer matches. BrowserContextConfig.no_viewport (context.py:147) is still never read. Remedy: pass no_viewport=True in headed mode and respect self.config.no_viewport; set viewport=browser_window_size only for headless.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Removing the attachShadow open-mode override hides closed shadow-DOM content from DOM extraction
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: buildDomTree.js:977 walks shadow trees only through node.shadowRoot, which is null for closed roots. Elements inside closed shadow roots (web components, consent/login widgets) no longer appear in the DOM tree the LLM sees, so the agent can't target them. Remedy: keep the attachShadow override, or switch to CDP DOM.describeNode with pierce: true. If dropping it for stealth is deliberate, document the lost coverage.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Public Page/ElementHandle/BrowserContext types moved from playwright to patchright with no compatibility note
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: page_filter callbacks and get_current_page() now use patchright classes. examples/custom-functions/action_filters.py:23 and tests/test_action_filters.py:4 still use playwright's Page. User isinstance(page, playwright Page) checks and `except playwright.async_api.TimeoutError` handlers stop matching, and because playwright stays installed nothing surfaces at import time. Remedy: re-export the driver types from a browser_use module, update the example and test imports, and document the switch (exceptions included) in the release notes.

review_output.summary: [Medium] Patchright added but playwright kept as a runtime dependency; partial swap with no single alias module
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: no browser_use runtime module imports playwright any more. Only tests and examples do (tests/test_browser.py:6, tests/test_action_filters.py:4, examples/custom-functions/action_filters.py:23). Every install pulls two driver stacks, the install docs set up browsers for the copy the library no longer uses, and the driver choice is hard-coded in 7 modules. Remedy: add one internal driver-alias module, move the remaining imports to it, drop playwright from the runtime deps (or keep it only as a dev extra), and update the install docs.

review_output.summary: [Low] browser_binary_path move from alias= to validation_alias= has no test
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: nothing checks that the legacy chrome_instance_path / browser_instance_path names, or the field name itself, still populate browser_binary_path, so an alias regression would go unseen. Remedy: add a parametrized test over the three names asserting BrowserConfig(**{name: '/x/chrome'}).browser_binary_path == '/x/chrome'.

review_output.summary: [Low] user_agent now defaults to None: headless sends the native HeadlessChrome UA, and docs still show the old default
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: headless contexts now send Chrome's default user agent containing 'HeadlessChrome', which makes detection easier and works against this anti-detection change. The docstring at context.py:93 and docs/customize/browser-settings.mdx:122 still document the Chrome/85 string as the default. Remedy: in headless mode with no user agent configured, derive one with HeadlessChrome replaced by Chrome, and update the docstring and docs to say None.

review_output.summary: [Low] Conditional dict-splat replaces two plain boolean kwargs (same behaviour) beside a separate kwargs dict
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: the splat behaves exactly like the old bypass_csp=disable_security / ignore_https_errors=disable_security, despite the commit's "fix CSP" claim. One new_context call now uses three different idioms to pass arguments, and no_viewport=False is redundant once viewport is set, so it is harder to see what gets passed. Remedy: build every conditional option in the one kwargs dict (an `if self.config.disable_security:` block), drop no_viewport=False, and pass **kwargs once.

review_output.summary: [Low] Stale "anti-detection scripts" comment; patchright logger not silenced
review_output.failure_scenario: Impact: only a notifications-permission shim remains under the "Expose anti-detection scripts" comment, which misleads anyone looking for where stealth is handled. browser_use/logging_config.py:118 silences only the 'playwright' logger, so patchright's logging may no longer be suppressed. Remedy: update the comment to describe the shim (or move the shim to a named constant), and add 'patchright' to the silenced loggers.

result_text:
The review verdict is **BLOCK**, driven by the code findings; the spec check was skipped. It found 15 problems: 3 High, 8 Medium and 4 Low. All 15 are recorded through the findings tool, one call each.

**High, all three confirmed by independent verifiers:**
- **Every launch now needs Google Chrome installed** (`browser_use/browser/browser.py:283`). The default `Browser()` passes `channel='chrome'`, but the README and quickstart still tell users to run `playwright install chromium`. On machines without Chrome, such as most CI and Docker setups, the first run fails.
- **Firefox and WebKit no longer work** (`browser_use/browser/browser.py:91`). The config still accepts them, but the same hard-coded Chrome channel is passed to their launchers too.
- **The new context-creation logic has no test** (`browser_use/browser/context.py:413`). This covers the viewport, user-agent and security-bypass branches.

**Main Medium findings:**
- **`Agent` overwrites the user's `disable_security` setting** (`browser_use/agent/service.py:261`). It changes the context-level value on the browser's config, which the caller may share.
- **The page no longer fills the window in visible-browser mode.** It now gets the library's default viewport, probably 1280x720, instead.
- **Elements inside closed shadow DOM disappear from what the agent sees**, because the script that forced shadow roots open was removed.
- **Public `Page` and exception types now come from patchright**, so user code written against playwright's types stops matching.
- **`pyproject.toml` lists both `patchright` and `playwright`** as runtime dependencies.
- **Test gaps:** the disable_security sync, the no-argument `new_context()` path and the new launch kwarg have no tests. The existing launch mocks also can't accept the new kwarg.

**What the review could and couldn't check:**
- All 11 changed files were examined, by the reviewers' own account. Six reviewers ran (correctness, API contract, security, tests, AI anti-patterns, maintainability). Security found nothing.
- Of the 11 findings at Medium or above, the top 8 were checked by independent verifiers and all 8 held up. The other 3 (closed shadow DOM, public type switch, dual dependency) went unverified because of the 8-finding cap.
- Some library behaviour is unconfirmed because patchright isn't installed and web access was denied. This includes the exact launch error without Chrome, whether Firefox/WebKit reject the Chrome channel, and the exact default viewport size.
- No spec was available. The PR body couldn't be fetched because `gh` needed approval, and the commit messages reference no issues.
